events.name: Passport Walk-in Day
events.description:
Need a passport for upcoming international travel? Join the TXST Passport Services Office for our Passport Walk-in Day!

This is a great opportunity to submit your U.S. passport application without an appointment. Applications will be accepted on a first-come, first-served basis in JCK Room 360, and all services will end promptly at 2:00 p.m. Whether you are applying for your first passport or need a new passport for future travel, our staff will be available to assist you and answer any questions you may have. 

Before attending, please review the required documents and fees on our website: Passport Services Office : International Affairs : Texas State University.

If you require accommodations due to a disability in order to participate, please contact (512) 408-6386 at least 72 hours in advance of the event.

events.name: The Cost of Knowledge: Building an Open Research Ecosystem
events.description:
How we create, share, and access knowledge shapes who can participate in research and who benefits from it. In recognition of International Open Access Week 2026 and the theme “The Cost of Knowledge,” this workshop explores how open research practices can help create a more accessible, equitable, and sustainable scholarly communication ecosystem.

 

Participants will receive an introduction to Open Science and explore practical tools and strategies for sharing research more openly, including creating and using an ORCID iD, publishing and preserving scholarship through the Institutional Repository, and sharing research data through trusted repositories. Attendees will learn how these practices increase research visibility, support collaboration, and help researchers retain greater control over how their work is discovered and used.

  • resume and cover letter guidance and review
  • graduate program statement support
  • job search assistance
  • exploring job shadow and internship opportunities
  • professional headshots

Monday, October 19 and Friday, October 23, 10:00 am to 3:00 pm
Career Café // Career Services // LBJ 502

Can't make these times? Career Services support is available throughout the semester. Book an appointment to meet with a staff member at a time that works for you.

 

Check out our full Make College Your Career event series this fall.

events.name: What To Do BEFORE Your Internship Search
events.description:
Before you start applying for internships, it helps you to know what you’re looking for. This interactive workshop guides you through key tools and reflection activities to explore your interests, strengths, and possible career paths. You’ll explore:

  • How your major connects to different careers 
  • How internships fit into your long-term goals 
  • Ways to “test-drive” career options early 

 

A great starting point for those exploring major, career, and internship paths. 

 

*Open to all students. Counts toward the Internships & Career Experiences Pathway in US 1100.*

Before you start applying for internships, it helps you to know what you’re looking for. This interactive workshop guides you through key tools and reflection activities to explore your interests, strengths, and possible career paths. You’ll explore:

  • How your major connects to different careers 
  • How internships fit into your long-term goals 
  • Ways to “test-drive” career options early 

 

A great starting point for those exploring major, career, and internship paths. 

 

*Open to all students. Counts toward the Internships & Career Experiences Pathway in US 1100.*

events.name: Unity Console Development
events.description:
Unity Console Development
This 2-session workshop introduces students to developing games for console platforms (PS5, Xbox, Switch) using Unity. Students will set up the Unity editor and build environment for console-style development, create a basic game with controller input, and learn the real-world steps involved in publishing a game to console platforms.

Session Breakdown:

  • Session 1 - Foundations: Students will set up the Unity editor, project, and build settings for console-style development, then build a basic game with functioning controller input.
  • Session 2 - Publishing: A presentation covering the actual steps and requirements for publishing a game to console platforms, followed by open work time for students to continue developing their game for the remainder of the session.

Topics Include:

  • Unity Editor and Build Setup for Console Development
  • Connecting Inputs to a Controller
  • Basic Game Functionality and Testing
  • The Console Publishing Pipeline (Certification, Platform Requirements, Submission)
  • Using AI to Support Game Development

Students are encouraged to use AI tools to help develop their games, with a focus on achieving a base game project to build off of.

This course is in-person only. Some basic experience with Unity and/or C# is recommended.

events.name: Audio Capture and Virtual Production | Virtual Production and Filmmaking Best Practices: Part 3
events.description:
Learn how to prepare for a shoot, effectively use a camera, utilize lighting equipment and techniques, capture clear audio, and learn best practices for filming on an LED volume. Students will learn these practices in a classroom setting and then spend the second half of the workshop in the Virtual Production studio using these skills hands on. No prior experience necessary.

Part 3 Audio Capture and Virtual Production will cover the following: Audio equipment, audio balancing and syncing, the benefits/limitations of filming in a studio, genlock, moire, lighting for virtual production, and hands on practice in the studio.

The class will meet twice a week for two weeks. You must attend all four sessions to earn the micro-credential.

Part 1: Pre-Production and Composition - 10/13/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Part 2: Cinema Cameras and Lighting - 10/15/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Part 3: Audio Capture and Virtual Production - 10/20/2026 - 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Part 4: Mock Virtual Production Shoot - 10/22/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Upon completion of this workshop, you will receive a micro-credential badge in Canvas.

events.name: Koko's Glow Run
events.description:
Koko is taking over Boko's Glow Run and she's painting it PINK for Breast Cancer Awareness! 

Grab your glow sticks and neon paint for a fun campus run filled with music, glow stations, and good vibes. Whether you're a seasoned runner or just in it for the fun, Texas State Students, Staff and Faculty are welcome!

The route goes through campus and is approximately 2.33 miles. A map of the route can be found on map my run.

6:30 PM – Check-in & pre-race fun (yard games, photo ops, glow painting)
8:00 PM – Race starts!

What’s included:

  • First 900 finishers get an exclusive Boko’s Glow Run medal
  • Free pink glow gear (necklaces, bracelets)
  • Running bibs for all participants
  • Pre-race activities and vendors with free stuff!
  • Water at halfway point
  • Post-race snacks, drinks and recovery station sponsored by Coca Cola!

Please leave pets at home for this event.

Register your organization to become a Glow Station and cheer on runners along the route.  2026 Koko's Glow Run - RSO Sign Up for Glow Stations! Only 12 spots available! Earn Homecoming points and bring the energy.

Need volunteer hours?
Sign up using the 2026 Koko's Glow Run - Volunteer Sign Up Form to help with check-in, activities, snacks, or course support. 

We will be hosting a volunteer virtual info session on October 15, 2026 from 6 - 7 pm. Once you submit this form, we will add you to the invitation list for the virtual info session. Please join if you want to learn more about your volunteer role or the events operations! We look forward to having you volunteer and make Koko's Glow Run an unforgettable event for Texas State Students!

events.name: Open Closet Donation Drive 10/12 - 10/21
events.description:
Open Closet is a textile recovery program that provides free clothing for all Texas State University Bobcats! The Open Closet program includes a clothing drive that takes place at participating campus locations and a FREE thrift market at LBJ Ballroom on Tuesday, Oct. 27th from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM. 

The Open Closet donation drive runs from Monday, 10/12 through Wednesday, 10/21 as part of Campus Sustainability Month. Learn more about other events here: Campus Sustainability Month website.

 

We accept only gently worn clothing items. Donations must be free from rips, stains, and major damage. 

Accepted items include: Skirts, Dresses, Blouses, T-shirts, Tank-tops, Jackets, Pants, Jeans, Shorts, Hats, Ties, Scarfs, Gloves, Jewelry, Bags & Shoes

We do NOT accept: Damaged Items, Clothing with large rips or tears, Clothing with stains, Undergarments, Swim suits, or Socks

 

Find a donation location on our Online Map. Or see the list below.

Donation Sites Include: 

Evans Auditorium
627 N LBJ Dr

Ingram Hall
301 W Woods St

JC Kellam (JCK) First Floor
601 University Drive

Joann Cole Mitte Gallery Foyer
233 W Sessom Dr 

LBJ Student Center 2nd Floor
301 Student Center Dr

Physical Plant
151-2 E. Sessom Dr

Spring Lake Hall
201 San Marcos Springs Dr

Strahan House
626 Moore St

 

Visit the Official Open Closet website here.

If you have accessibility needs or any questions, contact the TXST Office of Sustainability at sustainability@txstate.edu.

events.name: (Round Rock)- Midterm Pumpkin Pop-Up & Hot Cocoa Bar
events.description:
Students are invited to take a well-deserved break from midterms by stopping by the Midterm Pumpkin Pop-Up & Hot Cocoa Bar, a cozy, drop-in event designed to support relaxation and recharge. Participants can pick up a mini pumpkin to decorate or enjoy a warm cup of hot cocoa or cider while taking a moment to unwind.

With a calm and welcoming atmosphere, along with light seasonal activities, this event provides a quick and accessible way for students to de-stress between classes. Whether they stay for a few minutes or longer, students have the opportunity to reset, connect with others, and return to their studies feeling refreshed.

Place: The Quad

Date: Wednesday, October 21, 2026

Time: 11am-1pm

events.name: Disability Lunch ’n Learn Series: Understanding Neurodivergence
events.description:
Join us for another Disability Lunch ’n Learn Series! This month, we’re focusing on ADHD and Neurodiversity!

This is a wonderful opportunity for Bobcats to come together and boost awareness about disabilities. So, students, staff, and faculty, why not grab your lunch and join us? We’ll be sharing our experiences, discussing different types of disabilities, and brainstorming ways to improve accessibility on our campus.

We can’t wait to see you there!

Join us for another Disability Lunch ’n Learn Series! This month, we’re focusing on ADHD and Neurodiversity!

This is a wonderful opportunity for Bobcats to come together and boost awareness about disabilities. So, students, staff, and faculty, why not grab your lunch and join us? We’ll be sharing our experiences, discussing different types of disabilities, and brainstorming ways to improve accessibility on our campus.

We can’t wait to see you there!

Prizes and giveaways are available while supplies last!  Enter to win a free DIPLOMA FRAME! Visit the Grad Fest website for more details.

events.name: Finding and Using Images and Media: An Introduction to Creative Commons
events.description: Celebrate Open Access Week! Come to the Finding & Using Images and Media: An Introduction to Creative Commons workshop to learn about copyright and openly licensed creative content, and how to find and use openly licensed images, music, and video and other open access content. Learn how to properly give credit or attribution to copyrighted or open access content and how to give your scholarly work, creations, and designs a Creative Commons license. Presentation tips and tech tools that can make your presentations and publications more professional and visually interesting will also be briefly covered. For faculty research, teaching, and presentation purposes and for student research and presentation purposes. Activities will be included. You can use the Canvas course to go along with this workshop if you would like:  https://canvas.txstate.edu/courses/2204760 This session is online to be more accessible and flexible.

events.name: Service-Learning Excellence Impact Fair
events.description:
Join us for the Service-Learning Impact Fair! This self-guided, drop-in event features interactive poster displays highlighting extraordinary community-engaged projects, student experiences, and partner collaborations from across campus.

Looking for ways to connect your academic major with real-world impact? Want to see what service-learning actually looks like in action?

Whether you have 10 minutes between classes or want to stay for an hour, drop by at your own pace!

What to Expect:

  • Self-Guided Poster Tour: Walk through compelling showcases of recent service-learning initiatives.
  • Printed Guides Available: Grab a guide at the door to navigate the exhibits and discover ways to get involved.
  • Major Exploration: Discover how integrating service-learning into your coursework can elevate your major, build your resume, and benefit local communities.

events.name: Research Internships
events.description:
There are many opportunities to gain paid research experience in STEM, environmental science, and social science fields. Programs such as NSF REU, NIST SURF, and NOAA Sea Grant provide hands-on experience and education to prepare you for a career in research. Attend this presentation to learn more about the application process, eligibility requirements, and benefits of these programs.  

Explore research internships on the IDEA Center website.

events.description:
Drop in with our Peer Navigators for personalized support as you get ready for registration! Walk through your registration prep, learn how to navigate holds and add courses, explore helpful resources, and get answers to your questions along the way.

Our Peer Navigators bring tips, support, and real student experience to help you understand the registration process, identify your next steps, and feel prepared when it’s time to register.

This is a registration prep workshop, so come ready to plan, explore, and get your questions answered before registration!

Students are welcome to come and go as needed. Plus, enjoy free food while supplies last!

events.name: Write Time
events.description:
Whether you're working on school assignments, crafting the next award winning screenplay, or getting closer to your thesis or dissertation goals, Write Time is the perfect place for you. We’re excited to support your writing journey!

We meet both in-person inside the University Writing Center and on Zoom. Sessions are 2 hours and consist of 25-minute work blocks with 5-minute breaks in between to help writers maximize productivity during the two hours. New writers are always welcome so stop in any time, we'd love to see you! 

Please email writingctr@txstate.edu for Zoom link.

If you require accommodation due to a disability, please contact our office 72 hours in advance at 512-245-3018 or writingctr@txstate.edu.

events.name: Grad College Shop Talk: Boredom vs. Laziness: Keeping the Mental Engine Running
events.description:
Do you feel unproductive at times or believe you should be doing more? This presentation is focused on identifying the difference between healthy boredom and the concept of laziness. In our current fast-paced lives it is important that we don't evaluate ourselves by the completion of our task list. This discussion will help you develop a well-balanced understanding of your experience and utilize your strengths in keeping the mental engine running.

Presented by Dr. Nicole Adams, Psychologist, Counseling Center &
Dr. Alicia Batshone, Psychologist, Counseling Center

Register today!

events.name: RHA General Assembly
events.description: A General Assembly is a meeting where all residents living on campus are welcome. These meetings serve as a time for all of Hall Council come together to conduct official business, share updates, and make decisions. During these meetings, members hear reports from the executive board and advisors, discuss upcoming events and programs, vote on proposals, and bring forward ideas or concerns from their residence halls. General Assemblies are also a space for professional and leadership development, as members gain experience in public speaking, collaboration, problem-solving, and decision-making. These meetings ensure that everyone stays informed, involved, and able to contribute to the growth of both the council and their own leadership skills, making them the central space for planning, development, and community-building within Hall Council.

events.name: Game Night at the RRC Library
events.description:
Need a break from the endless studying and screen time? Join us at the RRC Library in Avery 255 from 5pm to 9pm for an epic night of board games, laughs, and good vibes!
 
Whether you want to dive into one of our many library-provided tabletop classics or bring your own favorite game from home to share, there is a spot for you at the table. This is the perfect, low-stress chance to relax, recharge, and socialize with fellow students. Show up solo to make new friends, or bring your roommates along for some friendly competition.
 
No experience is needed—just bring your energy and get ready for a fun, casual night of gaming!

events.name: Unity Console Development
events.description:
Unity Console Development
This 2-session workshop introduces students to developing games for console platforms (PS5, Xbox, Switch) using Unity. Students will set up the Unity editor and build environment for console-style development, create a basic game with controller input, and learn the real-world steps involved in publishing a game to console platforms.

Session Breakdown:

  • Session 1 - Foundations: Students will set up the Unity editor, project, and build settings for console-style development, then build a basic game with functioning controller input.
  • Session 2 - Publishing: A presentation covering the actual steps and requirements for publishing a game to console platforms, followed by open work time for students to continue developing their game for the remainder of the session.

Topics Include:

  • Unity Editor and Build Setup for Console Development
  • Connecting Inputs to a Controller
  • Basic Game Functionality and Testing
  • The Console Publishing Pipeline (Certification, Platform Requirements, Submission)
  • Using AI to Support Game Development

Students are encouraged to use AI tools to help develop their games, with a focus on achieving a base game project to build off of.

This course is in-person only. Some basic experience with Unity and/or C# is recommended.

events.name: Intro to Open Source GIS with QGIS
events.description:
This workshop is intended to familiarize attendees with QGIS, a free and open-source alternative to ArcGIS Pro. The workshop will focus on completing common GIS workflows, including importing data, projections, attribute table editing, symbology, and creating map layouts. It will also touch on QGIS-specific topics such as plugins. 
 
Please read below:
 
This is a hybrid format workshop, offered both in person in the DataSpace Lab (ALK 452) online through Zoom. For all those interested in attending, please RSVP for this event. This will allow you to receive reminders and the Zoom link in your inbox as the event date approaches. 
 
*** If you are planning on attending remotely, PLEASE DOWNLOAD QGIS on your own machine BEFORE the workshop by following this guide we created. Note that QGIS is available for BOTH Windows and MacOS.

events.name: Mock Virtual Production Shoot | Virtual Production and Filmmaking Best Practices: Part 4
events.description:
Learn how to prepare for a shoot, effectively use a camera, utilize lighting equipment and techniques, capture clear audio, and learn best practices for filming on an LED volume. Students will learn these practices in a classroom setting and then spend the second half of the workshop in the Virtual Production studio using these skills hands on. No prior experience necessary.

Part 3 Audio Capture and Virtual Production will cover the following: Audio equipment, audio balancing and syncing, the benefits/limitations of filming in a studio, genlock, moire, lighting for virtual production, and hands on practice in the studio.

The class will meet twice a week for two weeks. You must attend all four sessions to earn the micro-credential.

Part 1: Pre-Production and Composition - 10/13/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - Classroom ALK139

Part 2: Cinema Cameras and Lighting - 10/16/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - Classroom ALK139

Part 3: Audio Capture and Virtual Production - 10/20/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - Classroom ALK139

Part 4: Mock Virtual Production Shoot - 10/22/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Upon completion of this workshop, you will receive a micro-credential badge in Canvas.

events.name: Creative Writers' Circle
events.description:

Come join us to socialize, learn, and be inspired by the multitude of voices and styles that make up the ever-evolving world of creative writing.

Please email writingctr@txstate.edu for Zoom link.


If you require accommodation due to a disability, please contact our office 72 hours in advance. 512-245-3018 or writingctr@txstate.edu

events.name: Do I Belong in STEM? Exploring Your STEM Identity
events.description:
You may use technology, data, science, or problem-solving every day without thinking of yourself as a "STEM person". But STEM skills show up in many fields. including Mass Communication, Health Information Management, and Agriculture, and they may play a bigger role in your future career than you realize.
 
In this interactive workshop, you'll explore what STEM identity means and how your experiences, interests, skills, and career goals shape the way you see yourself in relation to STEM.
 
Through short activities, self-assessments, and conversations with other students, you will:
 
* Discover how STEM connects to your major and future career.
* Identify STEM skills and strengths you may already have.
* Learn strategies for building confidence when working with STEM topics.
* Talk about imposter syndrome and why you don’t have to be a STEM major to belong in STEM spaces.
* Explore how your interests and abilities can grow as you gain new experiences.
 
You’ll complete a short STEM identity self-assessment at the beginning and end of the workshop to see whether—and how—your perspective changes.
 
You don’t need to be a scientist, engineer, or computer scientist to have a STEM identity. Come explore where STEM fits into your story.
 
This workshop is offered as part of the STEM-CLEAR identity cohort workshop series, supported by the National Science Foundation, award no #2345305.

events.name: Homecoming Service Drive
events.description:
Celebrate Homecoming by giving back to Hays County! We are collecting shelf-stable pantry items for Hays County food drive. Please see donation guidelines below. 

Spirit Stick Competition

Groups registered to compete in the Homecoming Spirit Stick Competition may earn points by donating items at the donation tent during designated Homecoming events or at the Leadership & Service Office (LBJ 427), Monday through Thursday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. We encourage groups to donate all items at once to ensure item totals are calculated correctly. Points are awarded based on each group's competition category, with point values corresponding to group size. Please see official rulebook for details. 

No participating in the Spirit stick competition? No worries, you are still able to donate!

Donation Guidelines:

  • Donations should be Shelf-Stable Foods (no frozen or refrigerated goods)
  • Must be unopened and have an intact label.
  • Must list ingredients.
  • Expired items CANNOT be accepted.

Suggested Donation Items (1 item = 1 donation):

  • Canned meats (tuna, salmon, ravioli, chili)
  • Canned fruits and vegetables
  • Canned tomato products (diced tomatoes, Rotel, sauce, paste)
  • Soups
  • Peanut butter and jelly
  • Pasta and pasta sauces
  • Macaroni and cheese
  • Shelf-stable milk
  • Cereal
  • Granola bars
  • Trail Mix
  • Pancake Mix
  • Oatmeal
  • Applesauce
  • Fruit cups
  • Bottled water
  • Rice and beans

events.name: 59th Annual Soap Box Derby
events.description:
The Homecoming Soap Box Derby is entering its 59th year as an annual tradition here at Texas State University. The purpose of the event is to promote school spirit and unity among the many organized groups that comprise Texas State University. The teams participating in this event build soapbox derby cars and compete for trophies and points toward the highly coveted Homecoming “Spirit Award.”

Organizations and departments who submit an entry to race their car in this event will be able to review the rules and regulations designed to provide uniformity of cars for a safe and exciting race. There is a limited number of soap box cars available that can be reserved on a first come, first served basis. Organizations who wish to construct their own cars will be able to review the construction requirements in the registration form and then attend the required soap box car inspection dates.

Student Organizations and University Departments wishing to compete in this year's Soap Box Derby must register your organization through this event form: 

https://txst.campuslabs.com/engage/submitter/form/start/735216 

Registration is open September 8-25, 2026.

listing.name: 59th Annual Soap Box Derby
listing.description:
The Homecoming Soap Box Derby is entering its 59th year as an annual tradition here at Texas State University. The purpose of the event is to promote school spirit and unity among the many organized groups that comprise Texas State University. The teams participating in this event build soapbox derby cars and compete for trophies and points toward the highly coveted Homecoming “Spirit Award.”

Organizations and departments who submit an entry to race their car in this event will be able to review the rules and regulations designed to provide uniformity of cars for a safe and exciting race. There is a limited number of soap box cars available that can be reserved on a first come, first served basis. Organizations who wish to construct their own cars will be able to review the construction requirements in the registration form and then attend the required soap box car inspection dates.

Student Organizations and University Departments wishing to compete in this year's Soap Box Derby must register your organization through this event form: 

https://txst.campuslabs.com/engage/submitter/form/start/735216 

Registration is open September 8-25, 2026.
 
If you require accommodations due to a disability in order to participate, please contact the Fraternity & Sorority Life Office at getinvolved@txstate.edu or 512-245-5646, at least 72 hours in advance of registering for this event.

events.name: Volunteer Opportunity: Nature Festival and Spooktacular Roots and Wings
events.description:
Come volunteer with us to help put on the Nature Festival and Spooktacular, a Roots and Wings event! The North Austin Community Garden is co-hosting this event with the Little Walnut Creek Branch Library and the Rundberg Alliance. The garden will be the site of our event and we will need volunteers to help with the food table (fruit, drinks and water coolers), the children's area (a free play sensory area), nature activities (leaf rubbing and seed balls). We really need the help, so please volunteer! There will be people there to help with any questions you may have and we will meet up before the event starts to go over roles and instructions. Thank you so much!!!

Volunteer Sign Up

Nature Festival and Spooktacular
North Austin Community Garden at the North Austin Y

1000 Rundberg Lane, Austin  78758

Sat, Oct 24, 2026, 2:45-6:15pm (CT)

 

Please note this is not a Texas State University Sanctioned event and no university staff will be present.

events.name: OFF-CAMPUS VOLUNTEER OPPORTUNITY: Viva la Vida Día de los Muertos Festival & Parade
events.description:
This is an off-campus volunteer opportunity that is not affiliated with TXST. No transportation is provided and all questions should be directed to Viva la Vida. More info: Visit their event page

Viva la Vida is looking for volunteers for their 43rd Annual Viva la Vida Día de los Muertos Festival & Parade on Saturday, October 24, in downtown Austin! Viva la Vida is Austin's largest and longest-standing Día de los Muertos celebration, and it's a great way for students to give back to the community and earn service hours, individually or as a group.

Viva la Vida's biggest needs are:

  • Morning set-up (6:00–10:00 a.m.): moving props from the museum and setting up the festival
  • Evening tear-down (6:00–10:00 p.m.): taking down the festival and moving props back to the museum

They also need help throughout the day:

  • 6:00–10:00 a.m. (festival set-up): Setting up props, tents, and decor
  • 8:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m. (festival set-up): Pulling out puppets and banners
  • 12:00–4:00 p.m. (festival assistance): Helping out on the festival grounds
  • 2:00–6:00 p.m. (festival operations): Helping out on the festival grounds
  • 6:00–10:00 p.m. (festival tear-down): Helping take down the festival

To volunteer: Sign up to volunteer here

Student organizations are also welcome to march in the parade as a group: Register for the parade here

More info: Visit our event page

events.name: Bus from TXST Round Rock to Football Game
events.description:
Ride to the TXST Homecoming Football Game! 🏈🐾

Heading to the TXST Homecoming Game? Let us do the driving! TXST students are invited to reserve a spot on our Homecoming Game Day Bus and cheer on the Bobcats at UFCU Stadium.

Transportation Schedule:

  • 3:30 p.m. – Bus departs from Texas State University Round Rock
  • Approximately 4:30 p.m. – Arrival and drop-off at UFCU Stadium
  • 10:00 p.m. – Bus departs UFCU Stadium
  • Approximately 11:00 p.m. – Arrival and drop-off at TXST Round Rock

⚠️ This event is open to TXST students only. A valid TXST Student ID is required to participate and board the bus.

Seats are limited, so sign up early and get ready to support the Bobcats at the biggest game of the season. Eat 'Em Up, Cats! 🎉🐾🏈

 

Sign Up 

If you require accommodations due to a disability in order to participate, please contact Student Success & Academic Services at 512.716.4001 at least 72 hours in advance of the event.

events.name: Education Abroad General Info Session (Online Pre-recorded)
events.description:
Interested in Studying Abroad?

Discover the possibilities of global education by attending one of our General Information Sessions, offered both in person and via Zoom during fall and spring semesters.

Prefer a self-paced option? Access our pre-recorded session anytime by selection Join Event Online link (Online Location) on the Bobcat Organization Hub site.

There is no scheduled time for this session - you can watch it at your convenience.

events.name: AI Literacy Workshop
events.description:
AI Literacy for Students

This workshop will provide an overview of how Artificial Intelligence (AI) actually works, giving students the awareness and background knowledge to use AI tools with more skill, confidence, and judgment. Students will experience how AI functions, discuss its real-world impacts, and learn where to trust, question, verify, or refuse a tool's output.

Topics Include:

  • What We Mean by AI: Generative Tools, How They Work, and Their History
  • Behind the Scenes: The Environmental and Infrastructure Costs of AI
  • Privacy and AI Agents: What Happens to Your Data and Conversations
  • Hallucination: Why AI Output Always Needs to Be Fact-Checked
  • Sycophancy: Recognizing When AI Tells You What You Want to Hear

This course is in-person only. No prior AI experience or programming experience is required.

events.name: Open Closet Free Thrift Market 10/27
events.description:
Open Closet is a textile recovery program that provides free clothing for all Texas State University Bobcats. The Open Closet program includes a clothing drive that takes place at participating campus locations and a free thrift market. 

Join us at the LBJ Ballroom, on the 3rd floor of the LBJ Student Center for free clothing -- donated by Bobcats and available for all TXST students, staff, and faculty!

You will need to provide your NetID to enter, and each participant is limited to five (5) clothing items.

 

To donate clothing for the market, check out the Open Closet Donation Drive. Bring your clean, gently-used clothes to one of our donation locations from Oct. 12th through Oct. 21st.

 

For more information, visit the official Open Closet Website.

If you have accessibility needs or questions, please contact the Office of Sustainability at sustainability@txstate.edu.

events.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) Internship Info Session
events.description:
Want to hear directly from the people who hire interns? Thought so – Career Services is offering a series of employer-led internship info sessions to do just that, connecting you to reputable employers. In these sessions, employers share what they look for in candidates, how their internship programs work, and what steps you can take now to stand out. You’ll get insight into: 

  • Real internship expectations and timelines 
  • Skills and experiences employers value 
  • How internships can lead to future opportunities

Our sixth internship information session will be with the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ).

Interested in building a career protecting Texas’s environment and natural resources? Join representatives from the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) to learn about internship and career opportunities and discover how students can gain hands-on experience working in environmental protection and public service.

What You’ll Learn

  • What to expect from a TCEQ internship or externship
  • Career opportunities across TCEQ and the environmental field
  • How students can gain hands-on experience through internships and job-shadowing opportunities
  • How TCEQ professionals apply science, engineering, policy, and other skills to protect Texas’s air, water, and land
  • How to explore current internship and career opportunities

Career & Internship Areas Include

  • Environmental Science
  • Engineering
  • Geoscience
  • Biology & Life Sciences
  • Chemistry
  • Water Resources
  • Environmental Compliance
  • Public Policy & Administration
  • Legal
  • Information Technology
  • Communications
  • Business & Administration
  • And more

Who Should Attend
Students interested in environmental careers, public service, science, engineering, geoscience, natural resources, policy, and related fields. Students from all majors are encouraged to explore TCEQ's opportunities, as the Mickey Leland Environmental Internship Program welcomes applicants from a variety of academic backgrounds.

What to Bring
Come prepared to learn, connect with TCEQ representatives, and ask questions about environmental careers and opportunities in public service. Students may also want to bring a resume and questions about internships, career paths, and the application process.

Learn More
Visit TCEQ's internship page to learn more about internship, externship, and career opportunities. TCEQ's Mickey Leland Environmental Internship Program provides paid, full-time summer internships.

 

*Open to all students. Counts toward the Internships & Career Experiences Pathway in US 1100.*

detail.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) Internship Info Session
detail.description:
Want to hear directly from the people who hire interns? Thought so – Career Services is offering a series of employer-led internship info sessions to do just that, connecting you to reputable employers. In these sessions, employers share what they look for in candidates, how their internship programs work, and what steps you can take now to stand out. You’ll get insight into: 

  • Real internship expectations and timelines 
  • Skills and experiences employers value 
  • How internships can lead to future opportunities

Our sixth internship information session will be with the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ).

Interested in building a career protecting Texas’s environment and natural resources? Join representatives from the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) to learn about internship and career opportunities and discover how students can gain hands-on experience working in environmental protection and public service.

What You’ll Learn

  • What to expect from a TCEQ internship or externship
  • Career opportunities across TCEQ and the environmental field
  • How students can gain hands-on experience through internships and job-shadowing opportunities
  • How TCEQ professionals apply science, engineering, policy, and other skills to protect Texas’s air, water, and land
  • How to explore current internship and career opportunities

Career & Internship Areas Include

  • Environmental Science
  • Engineering
  • Geoscience
  • Biology & Life Sciences
  • Chemistry
  • Water Resources
  • Environmental Compliance
  • Public Policy & Administration
  • Legal
  • Information Technology
  • Communications
  • Business & Administration
  • And more

Students interested in environmental careers, public service, science, engineering, geoscience, natural resources, policy, and related fields. events.name: Healthy Cats Tabling - "All Treats, No Tricks" Halloween Safety
events.description:
No tricks here, just treats! Join Healthy Cats for resources for a safer Halloween. Grab safer sex resources like condom packets, learn some helpful information for planning a safer night out, including information about alcohol standard serving sizes, signs of alcohol poisoning and drug overdose, nicotine/tobacco cessation, and how to calculate your Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC). Pick up some free naloxone and build your own harm reduction kit! Let's all have a safe and healthy Halloween!

Healthy Cats is a peer health education program focused on promoting individual areas of health and wellness.

If you require an accommodation to participate, please contact healthycats@txstate.edu a minimum of 72 hours before the meeting.

events.name: TKL Visiting Writer Series: Roxane Gay
events.description: Roxane Gay’s writing appears in Best American Mystery Stories 2014, Best American Short Stories 2012, Best Sex Writing 2012, A Public Space, McSweeney’s, Tin House, Oxford American, American Short Fiction, Virginia Quarterly Review, and many others. She is a contributing opinion writer for the New York Times. She is the author of the books Ayiti, An Untamed State, the New York Times bestselling Bad Feminist, the nationally bestselling Difficult Women and the New York Times bestselling Hunger. She is also the author of World of Wakanda for Marvel. She has several books forthcoming and is also at work on television and film projects. She also has a newsletter, The Audacity and once had a podcast, The Roxane Gay Agenda.

events.name: Write Time
events.description:
Whether you're working on school assignments, crafting the next award winning screenplay, or getting closer to your thesis or dissertation goals, Write Time is the perfect place for you. We’re excited to support your writing journey!

We meet both in-person inside the University Writing Center and on Zoom. Sessions are 2 hours and consist of 25-minute work blocks with 5-minute breaks in between to help writers maximize productivity during the two hours. New writers are always welcome so stop in any time, we'd love to see you! 

Please email writingctr@txstate.edu for Zoom link.

If you require accommodation due to a disability, please contact our office 72 hours in advance at 512-245-3018 or writingctr@txstate.edu.

events.name: Learn How You Can Bounce Back Academically! + Free Coffee/Snacks
events.description:
Join us to learn how it's not too late to succeed at TXST.

 

This session reframes failure as a learning opportunity and challenges the idea that bouncing back is something you do alone. You will practice reflecting on setbacks in ways that produce useful information instead of shame, then look at the social and environmental conditions that make recovery possible in the first place.

 

We'll treat resilience as a collective asset, one that grows through relationships, communities, and shared support, and discuss how students, classrooms, and organizations can build environments where both individuals and groups thrive.

 

After the workshop, stick around for free coffee & a snack before classes! Gateway staff will be there to answer questions and chat about how you can succeed next semester.

events.name: Registration Prep Workshop
events.description:
Drop in with our Peer Navigators for personalized support as you get ready for registration! Walk through your registration prep, learn how to navigate holds and add courses, explore helpful resources, and get answers to your questions along the way.

Our Peer Navigators bring tips, support, and real student experience to help you understand the registration process, identify your next steps, and feel prepared when it’s time to register.

This is a registration prep workshop, so come ready to plan, explore, and get your questions answered before registration!

Students are welcome to come and go as needed. Plus, enjoy free food while supplies last!

events.name: Halloween Party + Free Snacks!
events.description:
All are welcome! Come hang out at our 2nd social event of the year—there will be free snacks & other surprises!

About the club: Allied Scholars for Animal Protection (or ASAP) trains students of all majors to get active for animals with the vision of ending animal exploitation in all its forms. Our intention is to make veganism impossible to miss across college campuses worldwide. While many of our members are vegetarian or veg-curious, all are welcome—you do not need to be vegan to join.

We host documentary screenings, potlucks, social events, and volunteer opportunities, with a primary focus on (A) outreach and (B) career development. Our intention is to help all students connect their career to tangible systemic change in the animal rights movement. Come say hello!

events.name: Creative Writers' Circle
events.description:
The Creative Writers Circle at Texas State University, hosted through the Writing Center, is an in-person and Zoom-enabled community that welcomes writers of all genres and experience levels. Through sharing work, constructive critique, and engaging discussions, members not only broaden their own artistic vocabulary but also foster an environment of inclusivity and creative growth.

Come join us to socialize, learn, and be inspired by the multitude of voices and styles that make up the ever-evolving world of creative writing.

Please email writingctr@txstate.edu for Zoom link.


If you require accommodation due to a disability, please contact our office 72 hours in advance. 512-245-3018 or writingctr@txstate.edu

events.name: Making Better Maps
events.description:
Are you interested in improving your mapmaking skills? Would you like to learn some quick tips and tricks to instantly improve the quality and aesthetics of your maps? In this workshop, we will discuss a wide range of aspects and best practices for making digital maps, including use of color, fonts, labeling, symbology, and basemaps. We will look at examples from professional cartographers and discuss lessons we can learn to improve our individual maps. Basic familiarity with GIS and ArcGIS is required for this workshop. 
 
Please read below:
 
This is a hybrid format workshop, offered both in person in the DataSpace Lab (ALK 452) and online through Zoom. For all those interested in attending, please RSVP for this event. This will allow you to receive reminders and the Zoom link in your inbox as the event date approaches. 
 
*** If you are planning on attending remotely, PLEASE DOWNLOAD ArcGIS Pro on your own machine BEFORE the workshop by following this ITAC guide. Note that ArcGIS is not available for MacOS; if you do not have access to a personal Windows machine, please consider attending in person and using one of our workstations in the lab.

This is a hybrid format workshop, offered both in person in the DataSpace Lab (ALK 452) and online through Zoom. For all those interested in attending, please RSVP for this event. This will allow you to receive reminders and the Zoom link in your inbox as the event date approaches. 
 
*** If you are planning on attending remotely, PLEASE DOWNLOAD ArcGIS Pro on your own machine BEFORE the workshop by following this ITAC guide. Note that ArcGIS is not available for MacOS; if you do not have access to a personal Windows machine, please consider attending in person and using one of our workstations in the lab.

Although the race itself is relatively short, volunteers are needed to assist with the race course, distribute water to runners, and help with event setup before the race and cleanup afterward.

events.name: How Do I Network?
events.description:
Open to all students. Counts toward the Research Pathway in US 1100.*

Networking is a term that is casually thrown out in conversations with faculty and peers, but rarely ever explained. In this workshop we will discuss what exactly networking is, what it entails, and how it can affect your career. Additionally, attendees will have a chance to share their potential roadblocks around networking about networking and learn best practices for overcoming the struggle to reach out.

If you require accommodations due to a disability, please contact our office 72 hours in advance. 512-245-1515 or ideacenter@txstate.edu.

events.name: Pre-Production and Composition | Virtual Production and Filmmaking Best Practices: Part 1
events.description:
Learn how to prepare for a shoot, effectively use a camera, utilize lighting equipment and techniques, capture clear audio, and learn best practices for filming on an LED volume. Students will learn these practices in a classroom setting and then spend the second half of the workshop in the Virtual Production studio using these skills hands on. No prior experience necessary.

Part 1 Pre-Production and Composition will cover the following: Screenplays, Scripts, Storyboards, Shotlist, Shot Composition, Camera Movements, The Rule of Thirds, The 180 Degree Rule, and a brief introduction to the ALIAS Virtual Production Studio and the studio equipment.

The class will meet twice a week for two weeks. You must attend all four sessions to earn the micro-credential.

Part 1: Pre-Production and Composition - 11/02/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Part 2: Cinema Cameras and Lighting - 11/04/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Part 3: Audio Capture and Virtual Production - 11/09/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Part 4: Mock Virtual Production Shoot - 11/11/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

events.name: Blender 3D Bootcamp
events.description:
A beginner friendly workshop creating a robotic arm using Blender 3D.
NOTE: Workshop is 2 hours for 4 days. The following dates are November 2, 4, 9 and 11 from 2-4 pm. You must attend all 4 sessions for your micro-credential.
This NASA Badged workshop is introductory-level 3D modeling, unwrapping, rigging, and animation using Blender. NASA’s Scientific Visualization Studio works closely with scientists to create visualizations, animations, and images that promote a greater understanding of Earth and Space Science research activities: https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov.

events.name: Grad College Shop Talk: Writing for Human and AI Readers in the Job Search
events.description:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the job search process for applicants and employers. Many organizations now use AI-supported tools, applicant tracking systems, and automated review processes to manage large pools of applications. At the same time, job seekers can use AI tools to prepare stronger, more targeted job-search materials. Because these changes have emerged quickly, graduate students need practical guidance for understanding how AI is shaping the hiring process and what that means for the materials they prepare.
In this workshop, you will learn how resumes, cover letters, and related application materials may be read by multiple audiences, including hiring managers, search committees, applicant tracking systems, and AI-supported screening tools. Specifically, it will focus on practical strategies for using AI to improve clarity, organization, audience alignment, and responsiveness to job descriptions while keeping your materials accurate, specific, and grounded in your own experience. We will also discuss how academic job searches differ from many other hiring contexts and how AI can support your preparation even when automated screening is not part of the review process. You will leave with a clearer understanding of how AI is shaping the hiring landscape, how to prepare job-search materials for human and AI-mediated review, and how to use AI tools as part of a thoughtful, strategic writing process.

Presented by Dr. Timothy Ponce, Assistant Professor of Technical Communication, English Department

Register today!

events.name: Topic Tuesday: Funding Opportunities
events.description:
Growing a business often requires funding beyond your own resources.

This topic will introduce students to different types of external funding opportunities, including grants, loans, investors, pitch competitions, sponsorships, and startup funding programs.

Learn what funding sources look for and how to position your venture for future investment opportunities.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Topic Tuesdays is a new workshop series focused on researchers and innovators from campus and the community seeking to move technology-based ideas toward real-world commercialization.

Hosted at Star Park, the series features McCoy College of Business faculty sharing practical insight on entrepreneurship, innovation strategy, commercialization, funding, market validation, intellectual property, business development, and building technology-driven ventures.

events.name: AI Literacy Workshop
events.description:
AI Literacy for Students

This workshop will provide an overview of how Artificial Intelligence (AI) actually works, giving students the awareness and background knowledge to use AI tools with more skill, confidence, and judgment. Students will experience how AI functions, discuss its real-world impacts, and learn where to trust, question, verify, or refuse a tool's output.

Topics Include:

  • What We Mean by AI: Generative Tools, How They Work, and Their History
  • Behind the Scenes: The Environmental and Infrastructure Costs of AI
  • Privacy and AI Agents: What Happens to Your Data and Conversations
  • Hallucination: Why AI Output Always Needs to Be Fact-Checked
  • Sycophancy: Recognizing When AI Tells You What You Want to Hear

This course is in-person only. No prior AI experience or programming experience is required.

events.name: Cinema Cameras and Lighting | Virtual Production and Filmmaking Best Practices: Part 2
events.description:
Learn how to prepare for a shoot, effectively use a camera, utilize lighting equipment and techniques, capture clear audio, and learn best practices for filming on an LED volume. Students will learn these practices in a classroom setting and then spend the second half of the workshop in the Virtual Production studio using these skills hands on. No prior experience necessary.

Part 2 Cinema Cameras and Lighting will cover the following: Exposure, Camera Settings, Exposure Triangle, Lighting, Color Correction/Grading

The class will meet twice a week for two weeks. You must attend all four sessions to earn the micro-credential.

Part 1: Pre-Production and Composition - 11/02/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - Classroom ALK139

Part 2: Cinema Cameras and Lighting - 11/04/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - Classroom ALK139

Part 3: Audio Capture and Virtual Production - 11/09/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - Classroom ALK139

Part 4: Mock Virtual Production Shoot - 11/11/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Upon completion of this workshop, you will receive a micro-credential badge in Canvas.

events.name: Write Time
events.description:
Whether you're working on school assignments, crafting the next award winning screenplay, or getting closer to your thesis or dissertation goals, Write Time is the perfect place for you. We’re excited to support your writing journey!

We meet both in-person inside the University Writing Center and on Zoom. Sessions are 2 hours and consist of 25-minute work blocks with 5-minute breaks in between to help writers maximize productivity during the two hours. New writers are always welcome so stop in any time, we'd love to see you! 

Please email writingctr@txstate.edu for Zoom link.

If you require accommodation due to a disability, please contact our office 72 hours in advance at 512-245-3018 or writingctr@txstate.edu.

events.description:
Understanding how to fund your business is a critical part of growth.

This workshop will introduce students to banking basics, business accounts, loans, grants, investors, and other external funding opportunities available to entrepreneurs.

Learn how to prepare your business financially and position yourself for future funding success.

 

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Part 2/Second half of semester (October 21-Dec 2) is designed for movement to OPFT and C2C topic experts. 

Attend at least 5 workshops to pitch to earn consideration for the CSE Open Penny Founder's Table (OPFT) or Campus to Community (C2C) Launch Fund.

events.name: RHA General Assembly
events.description: A General Assembly is a meeting where all residents living on campus are welcome. These meetings serve as a time for all of Hall Council come together to conduct official business, share updates, and make decisions. During these meetings, members hear reports from the executive board and advisors, discuss upcoming events and programs, vote on proposals, and bring forward ideas or concerns from their residence halls. General Assemblies are also a space for professional and leadership development, as members gain experience in public speaking, collaboration, problem-solving, and decision-making. These meetings ensure that everyone stays informed, involved, and able to contribute to the growth of both the council and their own leadership skills, making them the central space for planning, development, and community-building within Hall Council.

events.name: ASYNCHRONOUS OPTION: Career Success Toolkit Assignment
events.description:
ASYNCHRONOUS ASSIGNMENT OPTION FOR US 1100 PATHWAYS – Complete prior to “event” deadline for credit  

 

In Canvas, join the Career Success Toolkit site maintained by Career Services. Complete the “Job/Internship Search” module in the Career Success Toolkit to build early career readiness skills.

 

You'll complete two assignments: 

  • Research whether your major requires an internship/co‑op and explore credit options 
  • Browse Handshake to find three jobs of interest and identify an upcoming career fair to attend 

 

 

Your work will be graded on completion and effort, and you’ll receive feedback after submission. If submitting earlier in this "event" timeframe, you will be in Round 1 of grading. Late October-early November, you will be entered into Round 2 of grading. 

 

 

If you have any questions, please contact Madyson Flint, Career Exploration Coordinator for Career Services and US 1100 instructor, at MLS332@txstate.edu. Be sure to leave enough time for a response (typically 2 business days).

events.name: How Do I Network?
events.description:
Open to all students. Counts toward the Research Pathway in US 1100.*

Networking is a term that is casually thrown out in conversations with faculty and peers, but rarely ever explained. In this workshop we will discuss what exactly networking is, what it entails, and how it can affect your career. Additionally, attendees will have a chance to share their potential roadblocks around networking about networking and learn best practices for overcoming the struggle to reach out.

If you require accommodations due to a disability, please contact our office 72 hours in advance. 512-245-1515 or ideacenter@txstate.edu.

events.name: Supervisor Development Day 2026
events.description:
Step Into Your Leadership at Texas State’s Supervisor Development Day!

Texas State’s Supervisor Development Day is a hands-on professional development experience designed to help supervisors lead with greater clarity, confidence, and consistency.

Throughout the day, participants will explore practical strategies for navigating the everyday challenges of supervision—from building stronger one-on-one conversations and communicating through change to developing employees, providing meaningful feedback, and addressing performance concerns.

Sessions will emphasize practical tools, real-world scenarios, and opportunities to practice skills supervisors can take back to their teams immediately.

This event is limited to 75 participants on a first-come, first-served basis. Participants must have at least one direct report to register.

events.name: Liberal Arts Virtual Career Services Office Hours (November)
events.description:
🌟 All Liberal Arts Students Welcome (Including Round Rock & Online Students!) 🌟

Fall semester is here, and Career Services is ready to support you! Whether you are away from campus or simply prefer the convenience of connecting from home, this virtual space is designed completely for you.

Join your Career Educator, Shekinah Wu, on Zoom for a quick 10–15 minute check-in to get your career needs addressed on the spot.

We can help you with:

  • Resume & Cover Letters
  • Networking & LinkedIn
  • Job & Internship Search (part-time, full-time, on-campus, or off-campus roles)
  • Interview Strategies
  • ...or any other career-related topics on your mind!

No appointment needed—just drop in and process your career needs!

⚠️ Please Note: We are hosting three virtual office hours sessions this fall. If you can't make it to today's session, no worries! You are always welcome to schedule a virtual or in-person appointment with me instead.

We can help you with:

  • Resume & Cover Letters
  • Networking & LinkedIn
  • Job & Internship Search (part-time, full-time, on-campus, or off-campus roles)
  • Interview Strategies
  • ...or any other career-related topics on your mind!

No appointment needed—just drop in and process your career needs!

⚠️ Please Note: We are hosting three virtual office hours sessions this fall. If you can't make it to today's session, no worries! You are always welcome to schedule a virtual or in-person appointment with me instead.

This is a hybrid format workshop, offered both in person in the DataSpace Lab (ALK 452) and online through Zoom.

events.name: 3MT® University Final
events.description:
Three Minute Thesis (3MT®) is a research communication competition in which master's students on a thesis track and Ph.D./Ed.D. students have three minutes to present a compelling oration on their research and its significance. The 3MT® promotes presentation and communication skills, provides opportunities and feedback for students to work on explaining their research to a non-specialized audience, and in general helps students hone their “elevator pitch” discussions of their dissertations (especially useful for those students heading into job interviews!).

At the University Final, twelve students will compete to win top awards. These students will be announced at the end of October 2026.

Guests who attend the event can vote for their favorite competitor and help them win the People's Choice award. Refreshments and snacks will be provided, and there will be time for a Q&A with the finalists following their presentations, door prizes, and raffle prizes. Join us at the University Final and help support graduate student research! 

Register today!

If you require accommodations due to a disability in order to participate, please contact 512-245-3451 or ods@txstate.edu at least 72 hours in advance of the event.

events.description:
This is an off-campus volunteer opportunity that is not affiliated with TXST. No transportation is provided and volunteers are encouraged to carpool. Questions should be directed to the Department of Organization, Workforce, and Leadership Studies (OWLS). You can email Rudy Hernandez, Aviation Lecturer at xwq35@txstate.edu

The 2026 Texas Capital Air Show is bringing heart-pounding, family-friendly fun and excitement to the San Marcos Airport this November. This is your chance to see some world-class pilots in action and unique aircraft up close! As a volunteers you help create a welcoming, memorable experience for guests while supporting the Wings & Warriors mission to eradicate suicide in our nation’s military members and first responders by being there for them in their times of need and providing them with any support and resources they may need. By giving a day or two of your time, you help make this event accessible, engaging, and meaningful for the community.

events.name: How to Read Research Articles
events.description:
Open to all students. Counts toward the Research Pathway in US 1100.*

One of the best ways to learn how to conduct research is by reading about the research other people have conducted. However, navigating research articles can be frustrating. In this session we will discuss the different parts of research articles, their purposes, and how to engage with them. Additionally, attendees will learn how to utilize two systematized reading strategies—SQ3R and PILLAR—to assist with annotation, comprehension, and reflection.

events.name: Alkek One Hackathon Kickoff
events.description:
Build something real in 72 hours! The Immersion Studio Hackathon is a team-based build sprint. You'll design and create a 3D user interface project in Unity, using the Immersion Studio's projection and interactive technology.

Details

  • When: Friday, November 6 at 12 PM to Monday, November 9 at 12 PM
  • Where: Alkek One Design Space (first floor of Alkek Library). Final projects are submitted online.
  • Who: Any Texas State student. New and experienced programmers are equally welcome.
  • Teams: Up to 5 people. Bring a team or find one in the Discord.
  • Prizes: $1,000 for 1st place, $700 for 2nd place and $300 for 3rd place

Get ready before the event: On Thursday, November 5, the Immersion Studio is hosting a Unity Basics + XR Integration Workshop in Alkek Library, Room 105. Each session runs about 1 hour, and you can join whichever one fits your class schedule: 11 AM, 2 PM or 4 PM. You can also stop by the Immersion Studio any time it's open to try the headsets and set up Unity, and find starter resources in the Discord.

How it works

  1. Build (Fri, Nov 6 at 12 PM to Mon, Nov 9 at 12 PM): Teams form and start building Friday at noon. Commit to your repository throughout the event, not just at the end.
  2. Submit (by Mon, Nov 9 at 12 PM): Submit your project at https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/0hwfGAFkXA with:
    • A demo video (3 to 5 minutes) showing your project in action, including a short segment where team members explain how a key part of the code works
    • A link to your project repository
  3. Judging: Judges review all submissions and score them on novelty, technical execution, presentation and collaboration.
  4. Finalist Q&A: Top teams are invited to a short Q&A, about 10 minutes per team. Each team walks through its project, and every member should be ready to explain how their code works.
  5. Results: Winners are announced in the Discord and by email.

Using AI: AI coding assistants are welcome, as long as you understand and can explain the code you submit. Finalists will be asked about their code, so make sure every team member knows how the project works.

Beyond the Hackathon: The first-place team will have the opportunity to further develop its project toward submission to the 3DUI Contest at IEEE VR 2027, an international competition for 3D user interface design. Guidance and support will come from the Immersion Studio and the Texas State XPI Lab.

Join the Discord: https://discord.com/invite/PBQj2BFsD

Hosted by the Immersion Studio (ALIAS) in collaboration with the Texas State XPI Lab.

events.name: OFF-CAMPUS VOLUNTEER OPPORTUNITY: Texas Capital Air Show, sponsored by the Wing & Warriors Foundation
events.description:
This is an off-campus volunteer opportunity that is not affiliated with TXST. No transportation is provided and volunteers are encouraged to carpool. Questions should be directed to the Department of Organization, Workforce, and Leadership Studies (OWLS). You can email Rudy Hernandez, Aviation Lecturer at xwq35@txstate.edu

The 2026 Texas Capital Air Show is bringing heart-pounding, family-friendly fun and excitement to the San Marcos Airport this November. This is your chance to see some world-class pilots in action and unique aircraft up close! As a volunteers you help create a welcoming, memorable experience for guests while supporting the Wings & Warriors mission to eradicate suicide in our nation’s military members and first responders by being there for them in their times of need and providing them with any support and resources they may need. By giving a day or two of your time, you help make this event accessible, engaging, and meaningful for the community.

events.name: Audio Capture and Virtual Production | Virtual Production and Filmmaking Best Practices: Part 3
events.description:
Learn how to prepare for a shoot, effectively use a camera, utilize lighting equipment and techniques, capture clear audio, and learn best practices for filming on an LED volume. Students will learn these practices in a classroom setting and then spend the second half of the workshop in the Virtual Production studio using these skills hands on. No prior experience necessary.

Part 3 Audio Capture and Virtual Production will cover the following: Audio equipment, audio balancing and syncing, the benefits/limitations of filming in a studio, genlock, moire, lighting for virtual production, and hands on practice in the studio.

The class will meet twice a week for two weeks. You must attend all four sessions to earn the micro-credential.

Part 1: Pre-Production and Composition - 11/02/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Part 2: Cinema Cameras and Lighting - 11/04/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Part 3: Audio Capture and Virtual Production - 11/09/2026 - 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Part 4: Mock Virtual Production Shoot - 11/11/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Upon completion of this workshop, you will receive a micro-credential badge in Canvas.

events.name: Unity Console Development
events.description:
Unity Console Development
This 2-session workshop introduces students to developing games for console platforms (PS5, Xbox, Switch) using Unity. Students will set up the Unity editor and build environment for console-style development, create a basic game with controller input, and learn the real-world steps involved in publishing a game to console platforms.

Session Breakdown:

  • Session 1 - Foundations: Students will set up the Unity editor, project, and build settings for console-style development, then build a basic game with functioning controller input.
  • Session 2 - Publishing: A presentation covering the actual steps and requirements for publishing a game to console platforms, followed by open work time for students to continue developing their game for the remainder of the session.

Topics Include:

  • Unity Editor and Build Setup for Console Development
  • Connecting Inputs to a Controller
  • Basic Game Functionality and Testing
  • The Console Publishing Pipeline (Certification, Platform Requirements, Submission)
  • Using AI to Support Game Development

Students are encouraged to use AI tools to help develop their games, with a focus on achieving a base game project to build off of.

This course is in-person only. Some basic experience with Unity and/or C# is recommended.

(The negotiation of job offers will be covered in a separate session).


Presented by Dr. Patti Giuffre, Associate Dean, The Graduate College

Register today!

events.name: Check Mate!  Chess at the RRC Library
events.description:
Looking for a fun way to unplug, relax, and meet new people? Join us at the RRC Library in Avery 255 from 5pm to 9pm for a casual evening of strategy, laughs, and good conversation!
 
Whether you want to test your skills, learn a few opening moves, or just hang out, this is the perfect low-stress environment to recharge and socialize with fellow students. Absolutely zero chess experience is required—we welcome complete beginners and seasoned players alike! Come on your own to make new friends, or grab your roommates for some friendly matchups. You can jump into a game with one of our sets or bring your own favorite board from home to share.
 
Show up whenever you can, grab a seat, and get ready for a fun, welcoming night of gaming!

events.name: Grad College Shop Talk: Breaking it Down: Introduction to Graduate-Level Research Writing
events.description:
This Shop Talk introduces writers to graduate-level writing expectations. It addresses graduate-level research writing with a focus on the general structure of research-based assignments such as research proposals and research studies for comprehensive exams, theses, or dissertations. Attendees will learn about the parts of these documents, the logic behind how they are written, and how to assess samples of research writing for their strengths and weaknesses in meeting the expectations of the genre. Although writing up literature reviews, methods, results, and conclusions will be discussed, this Shop Talk will serve as a broad overview of the genre.

Presented by Dr. Sarah Hart Micke, Director, University Writing Center

Register today!

events.name: Mock Virtual Production Shoot | Virtual Production and Filmmaking Best Practices: Part 4
events.description:
Learn how to prepare for a shoot, effectively use a camera, utilize lighting equipment and techniques, capture clear audio, and learn best practices for filming on an LED volume. Students will learn these practices in a classroom setting and then spend the second half of the workshop in the Virtual Production studio using these skills hands on. No prior experience necessary.

Part 3 Audio Capture and Virtual Production will cover the following: Audio equipment, audio balancing and syncing, the benefits/limitations of filming in a studio, genlock, moire, lighting for virtual production, and hands on practice in the studio.

The class will meet twice a week for two weeks. You must attend all four sessions to earn the micro-credential.

Part 1: Pre-Production and Composition - 11/02/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Part 2: Cinema Cameras and Lighting - 11/04/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Part 3: Audio Capture and Virtual Production - 11/09/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Part 4: Mock Virtual Production Shoot - 11/11/2026 2:00pm-4:00pm - ALK139

Upon completion of this workshop, you will receive a micro-credential badge in Canvas.

events.name: Write Time
events.description:
Whether you're working on school assignments, crafting the next award winning screenplay, or getting closer to your thesis or dissertation goals, Write Time is the perfect place for you. We’re excited to support your writing journey!

We meet both in-person inside the University Writing Center and on Zoom. Sessions are 2 hours and consist of 25-minute work blocks with 5-minute breaks in between to help writers maximize productivity during the two hours. New writers are always welcome so stop in any time, we'd love to see you! 

Please email writingctr@txstate.edu for Zoom link.

If you require accommodation due to a disability, please contact our office 72 hours in advance at 512-245-3018 or writingctr@txstate.edu.

events.name: Unity Console Development
events.description:
Unity Console Development
This 2-session workshop introduces students to developing games for console platforms (PS5, Xbox, Switch) using Unity. Students will set up the Unity editor and build environment for console-style development, create a basic game with controller input, and learn the real-world steps involved in publishing a game to console platforms.

Session Breakdown:

  • Session 1 - Foundations: Students will set up the Unity editor, project, and build settings for console-style development, then build a basic game with functioning controller input.
  • Session 2 - Publishing: A presentation covering the actual steps and requirements for publishing a game to console platforms, followed by open work time for students to continue developing their game for the remainder of the session.

Topics Include:

  • Unity Editor and Build Setup for Console Development
  • Connecting Inputs to a Controller
  • Basic Game Functionality and Testing
  • The Console Publishing Pipeline (Certification, Platform Requirements, Submission)
  • Using AI to Support Game Development

Students are encouraged to use AI tools to help develop their games, with a focus on achieving a base game project to build off of.

This course is in-person only. Some basic experience with Unity and/or C# is recommended.

  • Session 2 - Publishing: A presentation covering the actual steps and requirements for publishing a game to console platforms, followed by open work time for students to continue developing their game for the remainder of the session.

Topics Include:

  • Unity Editor and Build Setup for Console Development
  • Connecting Inputs to a Controller
  • Basic Game Functionality and Testing
  • The Console Publishing Pipeline (Certification, Platform Requirements, Submission)
  • Using AI to Support Game Development

Students are encouraged to use AI tools to help develop their games, with a focus on achieving a base game project to build off of.

This course is in-person only. Some basic experience with Unity and/or C# is recommended.

events.name: Pseudoscience or Real Science?
events.description:
Open to all students. Counts toward the Research Pathway in US 1100.*

One of our tasks as researchers is to put high quality and well defended research out into the world, but unfortunately not everyone feels the same. There is a variety of arguments passed off as academic or scientific information that simply fail to rise to the level of rigor necessary for scientific discoveries. In this workshop attendees will learn how to distinguish pseudoscience from real science, see classic examples of pseudoscience, and learn about logical fallacies.

If you require accommodations due to a disability, please contact our office 72 hours in advance. 512-245-1515 or ideacenter@txstate.edu.

events.name: Service-Learning Essentials: Community-Engaged Theatre & Mental Health
events.description:
Looking for innovative ways to bridge academic coursework, creative arts, and meaningful community impact? Join us for an engaging session designed to introduce you to the essentials of service-learning at Texas State through the lens of community-engaged theatre.

In this multi-part session, service-learning program staff will introduce foundational program concepts and designated course options. Following the introduction, our featured guest faculty member will share insights from their service-learning course focused on theatre in the community alongside a student performance called State of Mind: TXST. Learn how their course adapts the framework of State of Mind, an interactive theatre and public dialogue initiative originating in Montana that uses performance to address mental health stigma, highlight local resources, and spark vital community conversations.

Whether you are interested in the arts, public health, or community advocacy, this session offers a unique look at how performance can be a powerful tool for social change.

What to Expect:

Part 1: Service-Learning Core Essentials (15 min)

Learn foundational concepts, student benefits, and how to identify designated service-learning courses.

Part 2: Guest Faculty Spotlight and Student Performance (1 hour 15 min)

Hear directly from faculty on using community theatre models to tackle complex issues, followed by a live student performance demonstrating how performance art can foster public dialogue, address stigma, and activate community voices about mental and behavioral health at TXST.

events.name: AI Literacy Workshop
events.description:
AI Literacy for Students

This workshop will provide an overview of how Artificial Intelligence (AI) actually works, giving students the awareness and background knowledge to use AI tools with more skill, confidence, and judgment. Students will experience how AI functions, discuss its real-world impacts, and learn where to trust, question, verify, or refuse a tool's output.

Topics Include:

  • What We Mean by AI: Generative Tools, How They Work, and Their History
  • Behind the Scenes: The Environmental and Infrastructure Costs of AI
  • Privacy and AI Agents: What Happens to Your Data and Conversations
  • Hallucination: Why AI Output Always Needs to Be Fact-Checked
  • Sycophancy: Recognizing When AI Tells You What You Want to Hear

This course is in-person only. No prior AI experience or programming experience is required.

events.name: What are Quality Resources?
events.description:
Open to all students. Counts toward the Research Pathway in US 1100.*

Every researcher relies on quality citations and resources to construct their arguments. However, what happens to your argument if the quality of your citations and resources are called into question? In this workshop attendees will learn the difference between primary and secondary resources, and how to differentiate between good and bad resources. Attendees will also learn about high quality references outside of just peer-reviewed articles.

If you require accommodations due to a disability, please contact our office 72 hours in advance. 512-245-1515 or ideacenter@txstate.edu.
