events.name: International Education: External Funding for Graduate Students
events.description:
Interested in learning more about external funding opportunities for graduate students to study or conduct research outside of their home country? Attend this special International Education Week event, which will involve three different sessions, tailored to specific audiences and purposes: Funding for Study and Research Abroad, Funding for Students Studying in the United States, and a panel of TXST External Funding Recipients. Registrants may attend any or all of the following 30-minute sessions:

10:00am - Funding for Study and Research Abroad
This session will provide a brief overview of some of the external funding opportunities available to help graduate students study foreign languages, teach English, and conduct research abroad. Although most of these opportunities are limited to U.S. citizens, we will also share strategies used by international students to pursue funded activities outside of the United States.

10:30am - Funding for Students Studying in the United States
This session will provide information about the approaches and tools used by international students to find external funding opportunities for which they are eligible. During this session, attendees will discover how to customize their funding searches, as well as learn about TXST international students who have received external awards.

11:00am - Panel of TXST External Funding Recipients
This event will conclude with a panel discussion about the successful strategies that TXST awardees have deployed in their own planning, searching, and application processes. Join us to hear from these external funding recipients about their experiences and advice in seeking international education!

 

Presented by Dr. Andrea Hilkovitz, External Funding Specialist, The Graduate College &
Dr. Brian Smith, External Funding Specialist, The Graduate College

 

Register today!

events.name: Topic Tuesday: Developing Your Pitch
events.description:
Great pitches tell a clear and compelling story.

This topic will help students understand the core structure of an effective pitch by focusing on the “why” behind the idea, the problem being solved, the proposed solution, and the desired outcome.

Learn how to organize your thoughts and communicate your vision with confidence and clarity.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Topic Tuesdays is a new workshop series focused on researchers and innovators from campus and the community seeking to move technology-based ideas toward real-world commercialization.

Hosted at Star Park, the series features McCoy College of Business faculty sharing practical insight on entrepreneurship, innovation strategy, commercialization, funding, market validation, intellectual property, business development, and building technology-driven ventures.

events.name: Flag Parade (International Education Week Celebration)
events.description:
• Wednesday, November 18 (IEW) International Flag Parade

At Texas State University, the Flag Parade is a signature event that celebrates the diversity of the international student community. Students sign up in advance to represent their home countries and are provided with or bring their national flags.

Participants gather at a designated starting point and walk together across campus in a coordinated procession, often accompanied by music and announcements recognizing each country. As each group passes, their country is introduced, creating a moment of pride and recognition.

The parade typically concludes at a central campus location where students, staff, and faculty come together to celebrate, take photos, and continue building a sense of global community at TXST.

Place:  Meet at: ISSS in JCK 314 - 3rd floor and walk to LBJ Mall Area

Date: Wednesday, November 18, 2026

Time: 11:30am-1:30pm

events.name: Write Time
events.description:
Whether you're working on school assignments, crafting the next award winning screenplay, or getting closer to your thesis or dissertation goals, Write Time is the perfect place for you. We’re excited to support your writing journey!

We meet both in-person inside the University Writing Center and on Zoom. Sessions are 2 hours and consist of 25-minute work blocks with 5-minute breaks in between to help writers maximize productivity during the two hours. New writers are always welcome so stop in any time, we'd love to see you! 

Please email writingctr@txstate.edu for Zoom link.

If you require accommodation due to a disability, please contact our office 72 hours in advance at 512-245-3018 or writingctr@txstate.edu.

events.name: RHA General Assembly
events.description: A General Assembly is a meeting where all residents living on campus are welcome. These meetings serve as a time for all of Hall Council come together to conduct official business, share updates, and make decisions. During these meetings, members hear reports from the executive board and advisors, discuss upcoming events and programs, vote on proposals, and bring forward ideas or concerns from their residence halls. General Assemblies are also a space for professional and leadership development, as members gain experience in public speaking, collaboration, problem-solving, and decision-making. These meetings ensure that everyone stays informed, involved, and able to contribute to the growth of both the council and their own leadership skills, making them the central space for planning, development, and community-building within Hall Council.

events.name: Imposter Syndrome
events.description:
Open to all students. Counts toward the Research Pathway in US 1100.*

Having an accurate self-concept is one of the most important factors for a successful researcher, as well as a successful student. Unfortunately, it can be difficult to give ourselves credit for the skills we possess and the talents we have spent years accumulating. In this session we will cover the importance of an accurate and balanced self-concept and the different types of social and academic capital we bring with us to the research setting (from Yusso and Tinto's work on student capital and persistence). Attendees will identify the types of capital and expertise they bring with them to their research experiences to construct a balanced self-concept. They will also discuss combating negative self-talk.

If you require accommodations due to a disability, please contact our office 72 hours in advance. 512-245-1515 or ideacenter@txstate.edu.

events.name: Thanksliving Potluck: All Are Welcome!
events.description:
All are welcome—dish not required to join!

ASAP is hosting what we call a “thanksliving” vegan potluck where we celebrate the lives of non-human animals! If you would like to bring a dish, please ensure it is free of meat, dairy, eggs, honey, and other animal-derived ingredients. Come hang out!

About the club: Allied Scholars for Animal Protection (or ASAP) trains students of all majors to get active for animals with the vision of ending animal exploitation in all its forms. Our intention is to make veganism impossible to miss across college campuses worldwide. While many of our members are vegetarian or veg-curious, all are welcome—you do not need to be vegan to join.

We host documentary screenings, potlucks, social events, and volunteer opportunities, with a primary focus on (A) outreach and (B) career development. Our intention is to help all students connect their career to tangible systemic change in the animal rights movement. Come say hello!

events.name: Service-Learning Essentials: Community-Engaged Theatre & Mental Health
events.description:
Looking for innovative ways to bridge academic coursework, creative arts, and meaningful community impact? Join us for an engaging session designed to introduce you to the essentials of service-learning at Texas State through the lens of community-engaged theatre.

In this multi-part session, service-learning program staff will introduce foundational program concepts and designated course options. Following the introduction, our featured guest faculty member will share insights from their service-learning course focused on theatre in the community alongside a student performance called State of Mind: TXST. Learn how their course adapts the framework of State of Mind, an interactive theatre and public dialogue initiative originating in Montana that uses performance to address mental health stigma, highlight local resources, and spark vital community conversations.

Whether you are interested in the arts, public health, or community advocacy, this session offers a unique look at how performance can be a powerful tool for social change.

What to Expect:

Part 1: Service-Learning Core Essentials (15 min)

Learn foundational concepts, student benefits, and how to identify designated service-learning courses.

Part 2: Guest Faculty Spotlight and Student Performance (1 hour 15 min)

Hear directly from faculty on using community theatre models to tackle complex issues, followed by a live student performance demonstrating how performance art can foster public dialogue, address stigma, and activate community voices about mental and behavioral health at TXST.

events.name: Game Night at the RRC Library
events.description:

events.description:
Open to all students. Counts toward the Research Pathway in US 1100.*

Ever had a professor say "this paper is really good. You should submit it somewhere," and have absolutely no clue what that means? In this workshop we will discuss how to find an appropriate journal for your discipline and type of submission, what the journal submission process looks like, where to get assistance on campus with publishing, and what to expect once you have finally made a submission.

If you require accommodations due to a disability, please contact our office 72 hours in advance. 512-245-1515 or ideacenter@txstate.edu.

events.name: AI Literacy Workshop
events.description:
AI Literacy for Students

This workshop will provide an overview of how Artificial Intelligence (AI) actually works, giving students the awareness and background knowledge to use AI tools with more skill, confidence, and judgment. Students will experience how AI functions, discuss its real-world impacts, and learn where to trust, question, verify, or refuse a tool's output.

Topics Include:

  • What We Mean by AI: Generative Tools, How They Work, and Their History
  • Behind the Scenes: The Environmental and Infrastructure Costs of AI
  • Privacy and AI Agents: What Happens to Your Data and Conversations
  • Hallucination: Why AI Output Always Needs to Be Fact-Checked
  • Sycophancy: Recognizing When AI Tells You What You Want to Hear

This course is in-person only. No prior AI experience or programming experience is required.

events.description:
CSE Catapult is an open, monthly Q&A and networking space designed to support students and founders at the earliest stages of idea development.

Each session connects participants to key campus partners, including Alkek One for prototyping and innovation, Student-Made for student ventures, OPFT and C2C for business development, and STAR Park for broader entrepreneurial support.

Whether you’re just exploring an idea or looking for your next step, CSE Catapult acts as a direct pathway to resources, connections, and opportunities right from the beginning.

• Tuesday, December 1 – Attorney for Students. Before You Go: Housing & Lease Check-In and Check-out

Students are invited to attend Before You Go: Housing & Lease Check-In, an informative session designed to help them prepare their living spaces and understand their responsibilities before leaving for winter break.

This session will cover essential topics such as lease obligations during the break, tips for securing and maintaining an apartment while away, and guidance on avoiding common issues like damages or unexpected charges. Students will also learn what to check before leaving, including cleaning, maintenance, and communication with landlords or property managers.

events.name: Topic Tuesday: Pitch Day
events.description:
Put your storytelling and communication skills to the test in a real, high-stakes setting.

Deliver your pitch to potentially advance to the CSE Open Penny Founder's Table (OPFT) or the Campus to Community (C2C) Launch Fund.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Topic Tuesdays is a new workshop series focused on researchers and innovators from campus and the community seeking to move technology-based ideas toward real-world commercialization.

Hosted at Star Park, the series features McCoy College of Business faculty sharing practical insight on entrepreneurship, innovation strategy, commercialization, funding, market validation, intellectual property, business development, and building technology-driven ventures.

events.description:

events.name: Write Time
events.description:
Whether you're working on school assignments, crafting the next award winning screenplay, or getting closer to your thesis or dissertation goals, Write Time is the perfect place for you. We’re excited to support your writing journey!

We meet both in-person inside the University Writing Center and on Zoom. Sessions are 2 hours and consist of 25-minute work blocks with 5-minute breaks in between to help writers maximize productivity during the two hours. New writers are always welcome so stop in any time, we'd love to see you! 

Please email writingctr@txstate.edu for Zoom link.

If you require accommodation due to a disability, please contact our office 72 hours in advance at 512-245-3018 or writingctr@txstate.edu.

events.name: RHA General Assembly
events.description: A General Assembly is a meeting where all residents living on campus are welcome. These meetings serve as a time for all of Hall Council come together to conduct official business, share updates, and make decisions. During these meetings, members hear reports from the executive board and advisors, discuss upcoming events and programs, vote on proposals, and bring forward ideas or concerns from their residence halls. General Assemblies are also a space for professional and leadership development, as members gain experience in public speaking, collaboration, problem-solving, and decision-making. These meetings ensure that everyone stays informed, involved, and able to contribute to the growth of both the council and their own leadership skills, making them the central space for planning, development, and community-building within Hall Council.

events.name: Panhellenic Council Tour of Homes
events.description:
Get into the holiday spirit with the Texas State Panhellenic community at our annual Tour of Homes on December 3rd from 6–9 PM! Bring one donation item per person to gain access to all eight Panhellenic sorority houses, beautifully decorated for Christmas.

Each house will feature festive activities, holiday treats, and plenty of photo ops as we celebrate the season together. All donations will benefit the Texas State Child Development Center, helping support families right here on campus. Come enjoy a magical evening of sisterhood, community, and holiday cheer!

If you require accommodations due to a disability in order to participate, please contact the Fraternity & Sorority Life Office at FSLife@txstate.edu at least 72 hours in advance of the event.

All donations will benefit the Texas State Child Development Center, helping support families right here on campus. Come enjoy a magical evening of sisterhood, community, and holiday cheer!

If you require accommodations due to a disability in order to participate, please contact the Fraternity & Sorority Life Office at FSLife@txstate.edu at least 72 hours in advance of the event.

events.name: TKL Visiting Writer Series: Cheryl Boyce-Taylor
events.description: Born in Trinidad and raised in Queens, New York, Cheryl Boyce-Taylor is the author of seven collections of poetry. In 2021, her verse memoir, Mama Phife Represents, won The Publishing Triangle’s Audre Lorde Award and honors her son, Hip-Hop legend Malik, aka Phife Dawg, of A Tribe Called Quest. Her latest collection, The Limitless Heart, won the 2024 CLMP Firecracker Award. Cheryl is currently working on her eighth collection of poetry.

events.name: DSS Monthly Meeting - April
events.description:
Join us for the Division of Student Success’ monthly meetings on the following dates:

  • Tuesday, September 1, 2026 – LBJ Grand Ballroom
  • Tuesday, October 6, 2026 – LBJ Ballroom
  • Tuesday, November 3, 2026 – LBJ Ballroom
  • Tuesday, February 2, 2027 – LBJ Ballroom
  • Tuesday, March 2, 2027 – LBJ Ballroom
  • Tuesday, April 6, 2027 – LBJ Ballroom

 

Each month, we invite you to take advantage of the opportunity to further develop your knowledge base, contribute to advancing our Division of Student Success goals, and meaningfully engage with your colleagues across departments.

 

Breakfast and networking will open at 8:00 AM, and each program will begin at 8:30 AM and conclude by 10:00 AM.

 

Information regarding presenters and topics will be updated closer to the upcoming meeting date as well as communicated via email.

events.name: 3D Space Planning with SketchUp
events.description: This workshop is for anyone who wants to learn more about basic space planning skills for your home, office, or other spaces. No experience with SketchUp is required to attend this workshop. This workshop is online to be more accessible. You can use the free online version of SketchUp for this workshop.
